method: Thirty editorial story itineraries for international drama and film fans. A title can have multiple story routes. Scene evidence and visitor advice are separated; durations are estimates, not live journey times.

routes.title: Lovely Runner
routes.hook: From Sol’s front gate to a riverside confession.
routes.credit: tvN · reproduced in Hey Roseanne’s location guide
routes.audience: A Filipina traveler based in California documented visiting these locations. TIME also selected the series as its best K-drama of 2024.
routes.audienceKo: 해외 팬의 실제 방문 기록과 해외 매체의 작품 평가를 함께 확인했다. 로맨스 팬을 대상으로 가장 먼저 시험할 후보.
routes.visitNote: Photograph homes from the public street. Café opening hours need a fresh check.

stops.name: Mongted café
stops.scene: The café exterior plays Im Sol’s house. The facing blue gate helps you recognize the neighborhood where their school-day story unfolds.
stops.sceneTitle: Sol’s home, just across from Sun-jae
stops.visit: Look for the entrance from the street, then stop for coffee if the café is open.

stops.name: Haenggung-dong lanes
stops.scene: Sol pushes Sun-jae against a wall to keep him from getting splashed. Their flustered moment was filmed in the lanes around her house.
stops.visit: Begin near Mongted and follow the neighboring lanes; the map opens the wider neighborhood.

stops.name: Hwahongmun stream bridge
stops.scene: On the small pedestrian bridge over Suwoncheon, Sun-jae tells Sol he likes her. Hwahongmun forms the backdrop.
stops.visit: Look for the small stream bridge in front of the gate, rather than the gate itself.

stops.name: Yongyeon Pond
stops.scene: Sun-jae teaches Sol to ride a bicycle along the paths beside Yongyeon Pond.
stops.visit: Follow the pond path below Banghwasuryujeong Pavilion.

routes.title: Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha
routes.hook: Market mornings, the hilltop boat and a sea breeze.
routes.imageCaption: Hye-jin and Du-sik’s wedding photos at the hilltop boat
routes.placeCaption: The boat at Sabang Memorial Park
routes.credit: Studio Dragon · still via KTO; location photo via KTO
routes.audience: An English-language Korea travel post specifically considers adding Pohang to a trip because of this drama. Another asks how to reach the locations without renting a car.
routes.audienceKo: 해외 여행 커뮤니티에서 이 작품 때문에 포항을 일정에 넣으려는 질문을 확인했다. 차량 이동 안내가 상품의 중요한 가치가 된다.
routes.visitNote: Book transport between stops. The boat and hilltop viewpoint involve uphill walking. Set dressing can change.

stops.name: Cheongha Market
stops.scene: Cheongha Market stands in for Gongjin’s market, including the settings for Bora Supermarket, Oyun Café and the hardware store.
stops.visit: Walk the market lanes and look for the central squid statue. These remain working premises.

stops.name: Yoon Dental Clinic exterior
stops.scene: The fishermen’s welfare center was dressed as Yoon Dental Clinic, where Hye-jin begins her new life in Gongjin.
stops.visit: View the exterior from the public street. Interior access is not part of this route.

stops.name: Sabang Memorial Park
stops.scene: The boat on Mugeunbong is Chief Hong’s hilltop retreat. It also appears in the couple’s wedding-photo scene.
stops.visit: Walk uphill from Sabang Memorial Park for the boat and coastal backdrop.

sources.label: Reddit · adding Pohang for the drama
Reddit · visiting without a rental car

routes.title: Goblin
routes.course: Where the sea meets the forest
routes.hook: Follow the forest confession and the seaside flower encounter.
routes.imageCaption: Jumunjin Breakwater, the iconic seaside filming spot
routes.audience: Viki’s international audience page shows a 9.7 rating at the time of research. This indicates an established fan audience, not measured demand for this itinerary.
routes.audienceKo: Viki의 해외 팬 평점으로 작품 선호를 확인했다. 꽃을 들고 장면을 재현하는 경험을 시험할 후보이며 코스 구매 수요는 아직 확인하지 않았다.
routes.visitNote: The forest and coast are separate driving stops. Avoid the breakwater when waves or access restrictions make it unsafe.

stops.name: Woljeongsa fir forest
stops.scene: The fir-tree path is the setting for Kim Shin and Eun-tak’s romantic forest scene, where they confirm their feelings.
stops.sceneTitle: A promise in the snowy forest
stops.visit: Follow the marked forest path. Snow depends on the season; the scene’s winter setting is not year-round.

stops.name: Jumunjin Breakwater
stops.scene: The breakwater is the setting for Kim Shin and Eun-tak’s seaside encounter, remembered for the buckwheat flowers.
stops.visit: Find the filming breakwater near Yeongjin Beach. Stay ashore if waves or access restrictions make the pier unsafe.

routes.title: Our Beloved Summer
routes.course: The long way back to you
routes.hook: Ung’s neighborhood, fortress walks and Yeon-su’s green gate.
routes.imageCaption: Jidong’s residential lanes near Yeon-su’s house
routes.audience: A CIEE study-abroad participant documented a dedicated trip to the show’s locations and meeting other fans there.
routes.audienceKo: 미국에서 온 교환학생의 촬영지 방문 기록을 확인했다. 조용한 동네 산책과 사진을 좋아하는 팬에게 맞는 후보.
routes.visitNote: Both home stops are exterior-only concepts. Keep entrances clear and respect residents.

stops.name: Choi Ung’s house exterior
stops.scene: The white-walled building appears as Choi Ung’s home, one of the recurring settings in his story with Yeon-su.
stops.visit: Enjoy the exterior from the street; do not assume the former café is operating.

stops.name: Hwaseong Fortress walk
stops.scene: Hwaseong’s surroundings connect the couple’s home locations and date settings. This stop explores the filming area rather than a single confirmed camera position.
stops.visit: Take the fortress-side path through Hwahongmun toward Jidong.

stops.name: Yeon-su’s house lane
stops.scene: The green gate beside Jidong Supermarket appears as Yeon-su’s home. The nearby rainbow mural recurs in neighborhood scenes.
stops.visit: Keep the lane and residents’ doorways clear when taking a photo.

routes.title: Itaewon Class
routes.hook: Find DanBam, then take in Saeroyi’s city skyline.
routes.imageCaption: The DanBam filming exterior as shown in KTO’s guide
routes.audience: Netflix included Itaewon Class among the K-dramas competing strongly in Southeast Asian Top 10 lists in 2020.
routes.audienceKo: 동남아 시청 반응이 확인되는 작품이다. 짧은 야간 산책에 식사를 붙이기 쉬워 첫 한국 여행객에게 제안할 만하다.
routes.visitNote: The photographed business name and façade may have changed. The course does not assume the filming restaurant still operates.

stops.name: DanBam filming exterior
stops.scene: Saeroyi and Soo-ah meet again outside the pub at the end of episode 2. The exterior becomes a familiar backdrop to his new start.
stops.visit: Match the building at 57 Noksapyeong-daero 40-gil; the current business may differ.

stops.name: Noksapyeong footbridge
stops.scene: On the pedestrian overpass, Saeroyi admits that he needs Yi-seo. The city lights and Namsan Tower frame the scene.
stops.visit: Cross the public footbridge and keep its walking lane clear.

routes.title: Vincenzo
routes.hook: Walk into the plaza, then follow the city after dark.
routes.placeCaption: Cheonggye building in the Sewoon complex
routes.credit: Studio Dragon · still via KTO; location photo via KTO
routes.audience: What’s on Netflix’s 2021 review reports sustained Top 10 presence in Vietnam, Japan, Thailand and Malaysia. This is historical viewing evidence, not a current tourism demand count.
routes.audienceKo: 2021년 해외 넷플릭스 순위 분석에서 아시아 시청 반응을 확인했다. 송중기 팬을 대상으로 도심 코스 수요를 시험할 후보.
routes.visitNote: Use public walkways in the working mall. Bank of Korea is an exterior stop; no interior scene access is promised.

stops.name: Geumga Plaza exterior
stops.scene: The Cheonggye building in the Sewoon complex doubles as Geumga Plaza, the central setting shared by Vincenzo and its tenants.
stops.visit: Explore public walkways around the working shopping complex.

stops.name: Bank of Korea exterior
stops.scene: The Bank of Korea’s historic building provides the setting for Woosang, the law firm allied with Babel.
stops.visit: This is an exterior stop. A museum visit does not provide access to the drama’s office sets.

stops.name: Seoullo 7017
stops.scene: The illuminated elevated walkway is where Vincenzo walks alone through the city at night.
stops.visit: Follow the pedestrian path above the streets near Seoul Station.

sources.label: What’s on Netflix · 2021 overseas viewing analysis

routes.title: Crash Landing on You
routes.hook: A reunion bench, a lakeside walk and a second love story.
routes.audience: Netflix reported the drama reaching Top 10 lists in the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan and Thailand.
routes.audienceKo: 해외 인지도는 높다. 한국 안에서 방문 가능한 재회 장면과 서브 커플의 장면으로 코스를 구성했다.
routes.visitNote: Plan travel to Chungju separately. Lighting and lakeside access can change with weather and maintenance.

stops.name: Jungangtap Park
stops.scene: Se-ri and Jeong-hyeok reunite with his men at Jungangtap Park during the South Korea part of the story.
stops.visit: Look for the filming bench along the riverside park.

stops.name: Tangeumho Rainbow Road
stops.scene: The lakeside bridge is the setting where the second couple share their feelings.
stops.visit: Walk the bridge around dusk; decorative lighting may vary.

routes.title: Extraordinary Attorney Woo
routes.hook: A temple path, a window through the rocks and time by the sea.
routes.audience: Netflix ranked the series first on its weekly non-English TV list for the week of August 15, 2022.
routes.audienceKo: 글로벌 시청 성과가 있는 작품이다. 제주 출장 에피소드의 장소를 묶되 직접적인 해외 방문 수요는 추가 검증할 후보.
routes.visitNote: Travel between the temple and north-coast filming spot by car or booked taxi. Hamdeok Beach can be an optional food break afterward.

stops.name: Gwaneumsa Temple
stops.scene: Gwaneumsa plays the fictional Hwangjisa Temple during the legal team’s Jeju business trip.
stops.visit: Walk the approach and temple grounds quietly; it is an active place of worship.

stops.name: Changkkom
stops.scene: At the window-shaped coastal rock, Jung Myeong-seok recalls memories of his wife.
stops.visit: Look through the opening toward the sea. Stay on accessible paths around the rocks.

routes.title: Squid Game
routes.hook: The everyday streets before the games begin.
routes.imageCaption: Paldo Dried Seafood, the shop used as Sang-woo’s mother’s store
routes.audience: Netflix reported Season 2 reaching the Top 10 in 93 countries in the week beginning December 30, 2024. This itinerary follows Season 1’s real neighborhood locations.
routes.audienceKo: 해외 인지도가 높은 입구 상품 후보다. 시장과 편의점 장면을 중심으로 하며 게임장 세트 방문을 약속하지 않는다.
routes.visitNote: These are working shops. Confirm the current business and get permission before photographing staff or customers.

stops.name: Baegun Market / Paldo Dried Seafood
stops.scene: Paldo Dried Seafood doubles as Sang-woo’s mother’s shop, which Gi-hun visits in the neighborhood outside the games.
stops.visit: Find the storefront inside Baegun Market; ask before photographing people.

stops.name: CU Ssangmun Uicheon filming site
stops.scene: After the first game, Gi-hun and Il-nam meet again outside this convenience store and talk over noodles and soju.
stops.visit: View the storefront from the public pavement. The business and outdoor seating may have changed.

routes.title: It’s Okay to Not Be Okay
routes.course: A quiet day by the sea
routes.hook: The hospital garden and the beach from their escape.
routes.audience: Netflix said the show spent over 100 days in the Top 10 in Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand in 2020.
routes.audienceKo: 동남아 장기 시청 반응이 확인된다. 바다와 카페를 좋아하는 팬에게 제안할 수 있지만 현재 현장 이용 조건은 재확인이 필요하다.
routes.visitNote: Check Secret Blue’s current operation and garden access before travel. Interior access and surviving set props are not confirmed.

stops.name: Secret Blue café site
stops.scene: The café grounds play the hospital exterior and garden, a recurring setting around Gang-tae’s work.
stops.sceneTitle: The garden at OK Psychiatric Hospital
stops.visit: Check the current café operation and garden access before visiting.

stops.name: Ayajin Beach
stops.scene: At the end of episode 8, Gang-tae tells Mun-yeong he wants to take a trip with her, with Ayajin’s sea in view.
stops.sceneTitle: A smile and a promise to get away
stops.visit: End with a walk on the public beachfront.

routes.title: Queen of Tears
routes.hook: A department store empire and the garden behind the family’s grand home.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: These are public venues used for selected shots; neither contains the complete fictional mansion or store.

stops.name: The Hyundai Seoul
stops.scene: The atrium and retail spaces stand in for Queens Department Store, where Hae-in leads the family business.
stops.visit: Explore the public shopping floors. The fictional rooftop is a separate filming location.

stops.name: Korean Stone Art Museum
stops.scene: The museum’s stone garden and exterior were used for the Queens family mansion.
stops.visit: Check museum admission before travelling uphill. Follow visitor paths in the garden.

routes.title: Business Proposal
routes.course: When the fake date becomes real
routes.hook: Flowers in the rain, then a carefree theme-park date.
routes.imageCaption: When the fake date becomes real
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: Allow a full day if you want rides. Flowers and theme-park admission are separate purchases.

stops.name: Yangjae Flower Market
stops.scene: Tae-mu buys Ha-ri flowers while they shelter from the rain at the flower market.
stops.visit: Start in the morning and check which flower-market halls are open.

stops.name: Lotte World Adventure
stops.scene: Ha-ri and Tae-mu’s amusement-park date brings them to the bumper cars and merry-go-round.
stops.visit: Admission is required. Ride queues can add several hours.

routes.title: King the Land
routes.hook: An island bicycle date and a photo beneath a heart-shaped tree.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: Gapado ferries depend on weather. Leave substantial driving time between western and eastern Jeju.

stops.name: Gapado Island
stops.sceneTitle: A bicycle date on the island
stops.scene: Gu Won and Sa-rang’s bicycle date unfolds on Gapado’s quiet island roads.
stops.visit: Book a morning ferry and check return sailings before renting bicycles.

stops.name: Sono Calm Jeju
stops.scene: The pair film King Hotel’s promotional video here and pose at the heart-shaped tree.
stops.visit: Ask the resort about garden access for day visitors before making the cross-island drive.

routes.title: Twenty-Five Twenty-One
routes.hook: A white gate, a tunnel and the little shop where friends gathered.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: The story is set in Seoul, but these scenes were filmed in Jeonju.

stops.name: Hee-do’s house exterior
stops.sceneTitle: The gate where they first meet
stops.scene: The white-gated house near the hanok village is where Hee-do and Yi-jin first meet.
stops.visit: View the gate from the public lane; do not enter the former guesthouse.

stops.name: Hanbyeok Tunnel
stops.sceneTitle: Love and goodbye in the same tunnel
stops.scene: The tunnel becomes a recurring place for Hee-do and Yi-jin to share feelings, and later to part.
stops.visit: Stay aware of passing traffic and keep the tunnel entrance clear.

stops.name: Ahyeon Supermarket set
stops.sceneTitle: A place to sit with friends
stops.scene: The group’s neighborhood store and bench were recreated here after filming ended.
stops.visit: Treat this as a reconstructed fan stop and check current access.

routes.title: True Beauty
routes.course: A secret shared between the pages
routes.hook: Follow Ju-kyung and Su-ho from the comic shop to the walk home.
routes.imageCaption: A secret shared between the pages
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: Bukchon is a residential neighborhood. Follow posted visitor hours and stay on public streets.

stops.name: Prince Comic Rental Shop exterior
stops.scene: This hanok storefront becomes the comic rental shop where Ju-kyung and Su-ho repeatedly meet.
stops.visit: The building is a real shop. Ask before taking photographs inside.

stops.name: Yunboseon-gil stone-wall lane
stops.scene: The stone-wall road beside the comic shop appears along Seo-jun’s motorcycle route.
stops.visit: Keep to the side of the narrow public lane.

stops.name: Sosho Gallery exterior
stops.scene: The gallery exterior stands in for Ju-kyung’s house during their walks home.
stops.visit: Plan for an exterior view only. Respect residential quiet hours.

routes.title: Hotel del Luna
routes.hook: Trace the hotel’s past, then visit a library of unfinished wishes.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: The two places represent different memories in the drama. Allow subway travel between Jongno and Jamsil.

stops.name: Hotel Seine café
stops.scene: Hotel Seine appears in the historical photographs that record the changing life of Man-wol’s hotel.
stops.visit: It is a café, not the full hotel set. Order if you use its seating.

stops.name: Seoul Book Bogo
stops.sceneTitle: The grandmother who wanted to read
stops.scene: The arched secondhand-bookshop aisles appear in the story of the grandmother ghost who regrets missing an education.
stops.visit: Check the bookstore’s current visitor notice before travelling across town.

routes.title: My Love from the Star
routes.hook: A trusted friend over coffee, then a promise above the city.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: Use the tower’s current access information for buses, cable cars and observation-deck tickets.

stops.name: Hakrim Dabang
stops.scene: Min-jun meets his longtime friend Lawyer Jang in this old coffeehouse to talk and play games.
stops.visit: This is an operating café with stairs. Order before settling in.

stops.name: N Seoul Tower
stops.scene: Song-yi and Min-jun embrace at the tower as their romance faces the limits of his time on Earth.
stops.visit: The outdoor terrace and the paid observatory have different access arrangements.

routes.title: Mr. Sunshine
routes.hook: Walk the streets of a changing country, then pause at the Glory Hotel.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: This is a walk through a purpose-built set, not a surviving neighborhood from the drama’s period.

stops.name: Sunshine Studio streets
stops.sceneTitle: The city where their paths cross
stops.scene: These purpose-built streets recreate early twentieth-century Hanseong for the drama’s encounters and political tensions.
stops.visit: Buy a studio ticket and follow the visitor route through the preserved set.

stops.name: Glory Hotel set
stops.scene: The Glory Hotel set represents Hina’s hotel, a meeting point for characters whose loyalties do not always align.
stops.visit: Both stops are inside the same studio. Ask which interiors are open that day.

routes.title: Kingdom
routes.hook: Enter the royal courts where a hidden illness becomes a struggle for power.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: These halls are real heritage sites. The action sequences also used purpose-built sets elsewhere.

stops.name: Tongmyeongjeon, Changgyeonggung
stops.scene: Tongmyeongjeon represents the queen’s quarters at the center of the palace conspiracy.
stops.visit: Check palace closure days and view the hall from designated visitor areas.

stops.name: Injeongjeon, Changdeokgung
stops.scene: The real palace hall provides a setting for Kingdom’s royal-court scenes and the struggle over the throne.
stops.visit: A separate palace admission may be needed. This route does not require a Secret Garden tour.

routes.title: Reply 1988
routes.hook: Two café dates from the quieter side of growing up.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: These are the real date locations, rather than the demolished neighborhood set.

stops.name: Taegeukdang main bakery
stops.scene: The bakery becomes the café where Sun-woo and Bo-ra drink Vienna coffee together.
stops.visit: Visit the original Jangchung-dong branch. Its interior has changed since filming.

stops.name: Brown Hands Dogok
stops.scene: This café is the setting for Jung-bong and Mi-ok’s date and first kiss.
stops.visit: Confirm current opening hours before crossing the river; order if you use the café.

routes.title: Alchemy of Souls
routes.course: Find your way back to Daeho
routes.hook: From the streets of the magical city to a reunion beside the stream.
routes.imageCaption: Find your way back to Daeho
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: Use the Mungyeong valley in the map search; other places have the same name.

stops.name: Mungyeongsaejae Open Set
stops.scene: The historical film set stands in for Daeho, the city where the characters’ altered fates meet.
stops.visit: Check studio access and allow time to walk in from the park entrance.

stops.name: Seonyudong Valley, Mungyeong
stops.scene: Jang Uk finds Mu-deok and embraces her beside the valley stream.
stops.visit: Stay on designated paths. Rocks are slippery, and rain can change access.

routes.title: The Glory
routes.hook: Follow Dong-eun from patient preparation to a reversal of power.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: The temple is an active place of worship. Scene descriptions reveal story developments.

stops.name: Cheongju Jungang Park
stops.scene: Dong-eun and Yeo-jung build a bond as he teaches her baduk beneath the park’s trees.
stops.visit: Use the public park paths and give local players space.

stops.name: Yonghwasa Temple, Cheongju
stops.scene: Hye-jeong kneels before Dong-eun and begs for forgiveness at this temple.
stops.visit: Keep voices low and avoid photographing worshippers.

routes.title: When the Camellia Blooms
routes.hook: Find Dong-baek’s bar and the neighborhood overlooking the port.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: Ongsan is fictional; the real neighborhood is Guryongpo in Pohang.

stops.name: Camellia bar exterior
stops.scene: This storefront stands in for Camellia, the bar at the heart of Dong-baek’s new life in the fictional town of Ongsan.
stops.visit: Businesses and signs may change. Check visitor access and photograph from public space.

stops.name: Guryongpo Park steps
stops.scene: The park steps above the port are one of the recognizable neighborhood backdrops of the drama.
stops.visit: Expect a stair climb and leave room for residents passing through.

routes.title: Parasite
routes.hook: Begin at a neighborhood shop, then follow the peach up the stairs.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: The Park house and the Kim basement apartment were constructed sets; this walk does not visit those homes.

stops.name: Doijissal Supermarket exterior
stops.scene: The neighborhood shop appears near the Kim family’s home as Ki-woo’s tutoring opportunity sets the story in motion.
stops.visit: Check the storefront from the street; it is not a movie-set attraction.

stops.name: Songijeong-ro stairs
stops.scene: Ki-jung climbs these stairs with the peach used in the family’s plan to secure another job.
stops.visit: The nearby stairs are part of a residential lane. Keep doorways clear.

routes.title: Parasite
routes.course: The long way down in the rain
routes.hook: Follow the family’s escape through stairs, a tunnel and a changing city.
routes.imageCaption: The long way down in the rain
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: The film edits distant locations into one journey. Travel between the two neighborhoods is needed.

stops.name: Jahamun Tunnel stairs
stops.scene: Ki-taek and his family descend toward the tunnel and pass through the pouring rain on their way home.
stops.visit: Visit in dry daylight. Use the pedestrian path and keep away from the roadway.

stops.name: Changsin-dong filming alleys
stops.scene: The film uses these steep neighborhood steps during the family’s rain-soaked return toward their flooded home.
stops.visit: The map points to the filming-area lanes; do not enter private stairs or houses.

routes.title: Decision to Leave
routes.hook: A detective’s pursuit through a city built on steep hills.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: This route focuses on the chase sequence. It does not include the film’s distant temple and beach locations.

stops.name: Choryang Ibagu-gil area
stops.sceneTitle: A chase that climbs the city
stops.scene: The chase sequence uses the neighborhood’s slopes and narrow lanes as the detective follows a suspect uphill.
stops.visit: Take breaks on the climb. This is a neighborhood walk rather than a guided film set.

stops.name: Chowon Apartment exterior
stops.scene: The pursuit reaches the stairs and rooftop surroundings of Chowon Apartment, where the detective catches the suspect.
stops.visit: View from public lanes only. Rooftop access is not part of this route.

routes.title: Pachinko
routes.hook: Two shores connect the girl who left with the woman who returns.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: Both stops are on Yeongdo. The coastal landscape remains, while the period village was dressed for filming.

stops.name: Taewon Pebble Beach, Taejongdae
stops.scene: Taejongdae and its pebble shore depict young Sunja’s hometown and the place where she works.
stops.visit: Check Taejongdae trail access and avoid rocks near rough water.

stops.name: Gamji Beach
stops.scene: Older Sunja returns to the coast with her son in a scene filled with memories of home.
stops.visit: Use public access paths and leave time to sit by the sea.

routes.title: Start-Up
routes.course: The day a dream becomes a company
routes.hook: Explore the two real places edited together as Sandbox.
routes.imageCaption: The day a dream becomes a company
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: Sandbox is fictional. Its screen geography combines separate places in Seoul.

stops.name: Oil Tank Culture Park
stops.scene: The converted oil tanks provide filming spaces for the start-up incubator where the young founders pursue their ambitions.
stops.visit: Check which tanks and exhibitions are open on the day.

stops.name: Nodeul Island
stops.scene: Nodeul Island supplies Sandbox’s island setting, connecting the characters’ business dreams with the Han River.
stops.visit: Check current construction and event access before visiting.

routes.title: Itaewon Class
routes.hook: From an apology in the neighborhood to Saeroyi and Yi-seo’s kiss.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: A separate story from the DanBam route, focused on the relationships around Saeroyi.

stops.name: Itaewon Children’s Park
stops.scene: Geun-soo apologizes to Saeroyi in this neighborhood park, recognizable by its bear-shaped slide.
stops.visit: Keep the playground available for children and avoid photographing them.

stops.name: Baekbeom Plaza approach
stops.scene: Their kiss was filmed on the path between the Sungnyemun-side entrance of Namsan Park and Baekbeom Plaza.
stops.visit: Walk the lower Namsan path. The scene is on the approach, not at the tower.

routes.title: The King: Eternal Monarch
routes.hook: Step into the bamboo portal, then follow Lee Gon back to the city.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: Allow road travel from Gijang to Haeundae; these stops are not one continuous forest-to-city walk.

stops.name: Ahopsan Forest
stops.scene: The bamboo forest is where Lee Gon discovers the gateway between parallel worlds.
stops.visit: Buy admission and stay on the marked forest trail. Screen props may not remain.

stops.name: Haeundae Gunam-ro
stops.scene: The busy street leading to the beach becomes the setting for a confrontation between Lee Gon and Lee Lim.
stops.visit: Use the pedestrian street and expect crowds in the evening.

stops.name: Haeundae Cinema Street
stops.scene: Lee Gon’s pursuit of the rabbit and Tae-eul’s solitary walk use this coastal street.
stops.visit: Finish along the waterfront path in Marine City.
